questions.question: What does the law of total probability state for a partition $B_1,\ldots,B_n$?
What kind of events must $B_1,\ldots,B_n$ be in the law of total probability?
options: A partition of the sample space

questions.question: What does the law of total probability do?
options: It breaks a probability into cases
It states that all events are independent

questions.question: Where is the law of total probability often used in Bayes' rule?
options: In replacing the prior by zero

questions.question: What must be true of the partition events?
options: Each of them has probability exactly zero.

questions.question: A test result is positive ($+$) or negative ($-$); $D$ is the event of disease. Which computation uses the law of total probability correctly?
options: Adding $\mathbb{P}(+\mid D)$ and $\mathbb{P}(+\mid D^c)$, unweighted, to get $\mathbb{P}(+)$
Splitting $\mathbb{P}(+)$ by disease status, weighted by $\mathbb{P}(D)$
Taking $\mathbb{P}(+)=\mathbb{P}(+\mid D)\,\mathbb{P}(D)$ for the sick group only
Splitting $\mathbb{P}(+)$ by the test result itself, $+$ or $-$

questions.question: If weekday has probability $5/7$ and weekend has probability $2/7$, what do these cases form for daily demand?
options: A partition into weekday versus weekend

questions.question: If shipping methods partition orders, why can late delivery probability be decomposed by method?
options: Each order uses exactly one shipping method case
Every order uses all of the shipping methods at once
Late delivery is not an event

questions.question: If $P(A\mid B)=0.7$, $P(B)=0.3$, $P(A\mid B^c)=0.1$, and $P(B^c)=0.7$, what is $P(A)$?
Why must the cases in the law of total probability be collectively exhaustive?
options: Otherwise the whole formula turns into Bayes' rule automatically
Otherwise some outcomes contributing to $A$ may be omitted

questions.question: Why must the cases be mutually exclusive?
options: Otherwise the conditional probabilities are all zero
Otherwise the same outcome can be counted in more than one case

questions.question: What is the role of $P(B_i)$ in the formula?
options: It weights the conditional probability for case $B_i$
It is always equal to $P(A\mid B_i)$
It is subtracted from every one of the conditional probabilities
It is the posterior probability after evidence

questions.question: A disease prevalence is $0.01$, sensitivity is $0.9$, and false-positive rate is $0.05$. Which expression gives $P(\text{positive})$?
Total demand is high with probability $0.3$ on weekdays and $0.6$ on weekends. If weekdays have probability $5/7$, what expression gives the total high-demand probability?
How is the law of total probability related to a weighted average?
options: It averages prior probabilities without conditional terms.
It always gives the unweighted arithmetic mean
It averages conditional probabilities weighted by case probabilities
It subtracts each case probability from one

questions.question: What goes wrong if a case $B_i$ has $P(B_i)=0$ in the displayed formula?
options: The partition cannot contain more than one event.
$P(A\mid B_i)$ is undefined by the usual formula

questions.question: Suppose three machine types have probabilities $0.2,0.5,0.3$ and failure probabilities $0.01,0.04,0.10$. What expression gives total failure probability?
If $P(A)=0.46$, $P(A\mid B)=0.7$, $P(B)=0.4$, and $\{B,B^c\}$ is a partition, what is $P(A\mid B^c)$?
